title: The Times Marks 175 Years by Celebrating Original Reporting
summary: To mark The New York Times’s 175th anniversary this week, The Times is honoring all journalists who do original reporting.
body_markdown:
‘Reporters follow the facts’ video honors all journalists doing essential work.


To mark The New York Times’s 175th anniversary this week, The Times is honoring all journalists who do original reporting. That difficult work — going to places, talking to people, digging up information, covering important issues and events — is what reporters at The Times and elsewhere are committed to today and into the future.


This morning, The Times posted “Reporters follow the facts,” a video that showcases how reporters unearth information that would otherwise remain unknown. The video features impactful Times reporting, from the Pentagon papers to Covid to #MeToo, and shows the skill and rigor that go into following the facts wherever they lead. It also includes some never-before-seen images from past Times reporting.


“Original reporting is essential, and getting rarer,” says Jessi Brattengeier, creative director for Culture, Communications and Live Experience at The Times. “For our 175th anniversary, we didn’t want to just look back. We wanted to make people stop and notice the work that makes the reporting possible and to remind them why it’s worth supporting. ‘Reporters follow the facts’ is a reminder of what it actually takes to get the story and what we all lose when no one is there to do that important work.”


> [@nytimes](https://www.tiktok.com/@nytimes?refer=embed) The New York Times turns 175 years old this week. “I fear we are careening toward a future with fewer and fewer journalists to do the expensive, difficult work of original reporting,” our publisher, A.G. Sulzberger, said in a speech this year. That difficult work — going to places, talking to people, digging up information, covering important issues and events — is what reporters at The Times and elsewhere are committed to today and into the future. We thank the reporters who have been a part of our history of independent journalism. And no matter where you get it, thank you for supporting fact-based reporting.[#independentjournalism](https://www.tiktok.com/tag/independentjournalism?refer=embed)[♬ original sound – The New York Times](https://www.tiktok.com/music/original-sound-The-New-York-Times-7686086377687075597?refer=embed)


This video is just one of the several ways The Times is calling attention to reporters and the essential work they do as part of the 175th anniversary. Happening now is[a college tour](https://www.nytco.com/press/the-times-takes-its-reporting-and-photojournalism-to-campuses/) that brings a photojournalism exhibit to campuses, giving students a glimpse at the hard-to-reach places where reporters do their work. Michigan State University is the next destination, on Sept. 29.


Later this fall, 12 Times runners, captained by C.E.O. Meredith Kopit Levin and Chief Legal Office Diane Brayton, will run the New York City Marathon as part of the Times’s Run for Reporting initiative. Times runners will raise funds for the Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism at CUNY’s free tuition campaign. Anyone can join the Run for Reporting run club on Strava and support CUNY or the journalistic nonprofit of their choice.
